selection_rationale: The selected papers cover the core dimensions of the research question: (1) Foundational and advanced RAG architectures (Iter-RetGen, DRAGIN, In-Context RALM); (2) Evaluation frameworks and benchmarks (RGB, MIRAGE, OmniEval); (3) Reliability and factuality (CRAG, Trust-RAG, Legal RAG evaluation); (4) Efficiency and cost (RAG vs Long-Context, SELF-ROUTE); (5) Training and coupling strategies (R2AG, Self-Reasoning, Domain-specific fine-tuning). The selection prioritizes technical evidence and empirical studies over purely application-focused papers, ensuring a robust coverage of the technical landscape.
anticipated_gaps: Few papers explicitly focus on the 'training' of the retriever itself (e.g., end-to-end retriever training) in the provided list, though R2AG touches on it.
Limited explicit discussion on 'computational cost' beyond the RAG vs Long-Context comparison.
Few papers address the 'evidence boundaries' specifically in the context of 'hallucination' vs 'truth' in a unified theoretical framework, though CRAG and Trust-RAG survey touch on it.

ranked.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey

ranked.authors: Zhihong Shao, Yeyun Gong, Yelong Shen, Minlie Huang, Nan Duan, Weizhu Chen

ranked.authors: Weihang Su, Yichen Tang, Qingyao Ai, Zhijing Wu, Yiqun Liu

screening.reason: Introduces DRAGIN, a dynamic RAG framework that decides when and what to retrieve based on LLM information needs. Directly addresses the 'training/decision mechanism' and 'coupling' aspects.

ranked.authors: Ori Ram, Yoav Levine, Itay Dalmedigos, Dor Muhlgay, Amnon Shashua, Kevin Leyton‐Brown, Yoav Shoham

ranked.authors: Jiawei Chen, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun
